title: Architect Overview
description: For tech leads and architects designing the React 19 / .NET 10 / Design System migration. Deep look at provider hierarchy, compound components, module augmentation, telemetry, CSP, and migration blockers.

steps.title: Bootstrap sequence — the provider hierarchy
steps.description:
**Situation**: Everything that wraps the React tree is assembled here before a single component renders.

**Mechanism**: The render tree is deliberately ordered:
```
MsalProvider        ← auth session (MSAL token cache, account management)
  AccountProvider   ← user profile state (org, branch, ToU, modals)
    StrictMode      ← double-invoke effects in dev mode
      RouterProvider ← React Router v6 (createBrowserRouter)
```

**Why this order matters**: `AccountProvider` reads from MSAL internally (via `useMsal`), so it must be a child of `MsalProvider`. `RouterProvider` renders route components that consume both MSAL and `AccountContext`, so it must be inside both providers.

**Implication for migration**: React 19 with concurrent rendering will make `StrictMode` double-invocations more aggressive. Every `useEffect` in every provider must have a cleanup function before upgrading, or effects will fire twice and produce duplicate API calls, duplicate event registrations, and double-fire telemetry events.

**Gotcha**: There is no error boundary wrapping `AccountProvider`. An uncaught exception in the provider's initialization renders the entire app blank with no recovery path.

steps.title: Route tree — 25+ routes in one file
steps.description:
**Situation**: All routes are in one file — this is a deliberate architectural choice that makes the routing contract visible and auditable in one place.

**Mechanism**: Three route categories:
1. Public `<Layout>` routes — no auth required (`/help-guide`, `/sign-out-helper`)
2. Authenticated routes with full chrome — `<AuthenticatedElement>` default (`/dashboard`, `/quotation/:id/*`)
3. Authenticated wizard routes — `<AuthenticatedElement displayHeaderAndFooter={false}>` for flows that manage their own chrome

Error display routes (`/server-error`, `/not-found`, `*`) use `<PreConditions displayHeaderAndFooter>` — they are accessible pre-auth.

**Implication**: When the Design System migration introduces a new page layout component, this is the single file to update for route-level chrome changes.

**Gotcha**: `displayHeaderAndFooter={false}` is a prop on `PreConditions` (nested inside `AuthenticatedElement`), not on `AuthenticatedElement` itself. The implementation flows: `AuthenticatedElement` → `PreConditions` → `displayHeaderAndFooter` controls whether `<Layout>` is rendered.

steps.title: Auth guard composition
steps.description:
**Situation**: `AuthenticatedElement` is a composed guard — three concerns layered via React composition rather than a single monolithic gatekeeper.

**Mechanism**:
```
PreConditions
  isAuthBypassEnabled() ?
    ErrorBoundary (ai.reactPlugin)     ← auth bypassed (dev mode)
      {children}
  :
    MsalAuthenticationTemplate (InteractionType.Redirect)
      ErrorBoundary (ai.reactPlugin)
        {children}  ← the route component
```

`PreConditions` handles ToU acceptance and account/contact setup gates — it redirects to the appropriate wizard if incomplete. `isAuthBypassEnabled()` short-circuits the MSAL redirect in local dev bypass mode. `MsalAuthenticationTemplate` triggers a B2C redirect if there's no valid MSAL session. `ErrorBoundary` catches any unhandled exception from the route component and reports it to App Insights.

**Implication for architecture**: The composition approach means each layer can evolve independently. Adding a new gate (e.g., feature flag checks) means adding a new wrapper inside `AuthenticatedElement` without touching `PreConditions` or `MsalAuthenticationTemplate`.

**Gotcha**: `RedirectToHome` (lines 15-25) handles route-level errors from React Router's `useRouteError`. On a `404` it redirects to `/not-found`; on anything else it goes to `/server-error`. The `instance.setActiveAccount(null)` call clears the MSAL active account before redirecting — this ensures the auth state is clean on error recovery.

steps.title: AccountContextState — the user state machine
steps.description:
**Situation**: `AccountContextState` has been split into two focused interfaces as part of Phase 5.1, with `AccountContextState` retained as a combined type alias for prop helper functions.

**Mechanism**: The context is now structured as:
- `AccountStateContext` — the read-only state: `isLoading`, `details` (`AccountDetails | null`), including org name, trading name, branch, ABN, ToU flags, etc.
- `AccountDispatchContext` — the mutators: `setAgree`, `setCompleted`, `setContactCompleted`, `setDefaultOrganisationId`, `setTargetOrganisation`, `setOrganisationAndBranch`, `setUserProfile`
- `AccountContextState = AccountStateContext & AccountDispatchContext` — kept as a type alias for prop helper functions that need both
- Two separate React contexts: `AccountStateCtx` and `AccountDispatchCtx`

**Hooks**: `useAccountState()` and `useAccountDispatch()` from `authentication/hooks.tsx`.

**Architecture note**: The split into `AccountStateCtx`/`AccountDispatchCtx` means state consumers that don't call mutations no longer re-render on mutation. `ModalStateCtx`/`ModalDispatchCtx` further isolates modal visibility from profile state.

**Modal flags moved**: `showBranchSelector`, `showRFQDeleteModal`, `branchSelectionModalMode`, `callingPath`, and `rfqId` have been moved to `ModalContext.tsx` (Phase 5.2). These fields and their mutators (`setShowBranchSelector`, `setShowRFQDeleteModal`, `setShowRFQSelectModal`) are no longer on `AccountContext`.

steps.title: WizardForm — compound component engine
steps.description:
**Situation**: `WizardForm` is the multi-step form engine used by every wizard flow in the portal (account creation, RFQ, accept quote, contact management, add branch).

**Mechanism**: It implements the Compound Component pattern:
- `WizardForm` iterates its `children` using `React.Children.forEach` (line 28) and validates each child is a valid React element
- For each step, it creates a `<Route path={step.location}>` that renders `<WizardRoutedStep>` — a component that handles value loading, validation, save/next/exit logic
- A wildcard `<Route path='*'>` (line 96) redirects any unknown path to the last step's location
- Navigation between steps is pure React Router — going to the next step is a `navigate(url + nextStep.location)` call

**Why this matters architecturally**: Adding a new step to any wizard flow is a matter of adding a `<WizardStep>` child. The routing, value loading, and navigation are handled by the engine.

**Note**: `React.Children.toArray` has been replaced with `React.Children.forEach` in a migration prep phase. The compound component pattern is preserved.

steps.title: WizardFormProps — the complete interface
steps.description:
**Situation**: `WizardFormProps` defines everything `WizardForm` accepts at the parent level — the values that apply to the entire wizard (not per-step).

**Mechanism**: Key props:
- `locationOnCompletion` — where to navigate after the final step submits (required)
- `locationAfterExit` — where to navigate when the user saves and exits (optional; defaults to `/dashboard`)
- `canSaveDraft` — shows Save Draft controls on steps that support it
- `confirmationOnSubmission` — optional `ModalProps` for a confirm-before-submit modal on the last step
- `showBanner` — shows the `<FormBanner>` with the RFQ reference number at the top of each step

`WizardStepProps<T>` (line 26) is per-step: `initialValues`, `onSaveAndNext`, `onSaveAndExit`, `validateHard`, `validateSoft`, `stepStatuses`, `loadStepValues` — the full async data loading + validation contract.

**Implication**: The 20+ props on `WizardRoutedStepProps` (which extends both) represent a large API surface. When migrating to React 19 or a new Design System, this is the contract to maintain backward compatibility for — all five wizard flows depend on it.

steps.title: Yup module augmentation — extending third-party types
steps.description:
**Situation**: The `declare module 'yup'` block extends Yup's `StringSchema` type with 17 Australian-specific validation methods without forking the library.

**Mechanism**: TypeScript module augmentation adds the type declarations. `Yup.addMethod(Yup.string, ...)` (from line 121 onwards) registers the actual runtime implementations. The module augmentation is in the same file, but they are separate concerns:
- The `declare module` block makes TypeScript aware of the new methods at compile time
- The `Yup.addMethod` calls register them at runtime — **only if this file is executed**

This is why the side-effect import is mandatory in any schema file:
```ts
import '../../validationSchemas/yupExtensions';  // executes the Yup.addMethod calls
```

**Implication for TypeScript 6**: TypeScript 6 may tighten module augmentation rules. Verify that the `declare module 'yup'` pattern still compiles. If Yup upgrades its own types and changes `StringSchema`, the augmentation may need updating.

**Architecture note**: Custom validators encode Australian business rules (AU phone format, AU postcode ranges, ASIC company name rules). These rules must be ported to any new validation library in the Design System migration.

steps.title: Telemetry — the App Insights singleton
steps.description:
**Situation**: `createTelemetryService()` is called once at module evaluation time (line 45: `export const ai = createTelemetryService()`). This is a module-level singleton.

**Mechanism**:
1. `ReactPlugin` is created and configured as an App Insights extension
2. `ApplicationInsights` is initialized only if `env.REACT_APP_APPINSIGHTS_CONN_STRING` is set and is not `'dummy-key'`; if the env var is missing or equals `'dummy-key'`, `createTelemetryService` returns `{ reactPlugin: null, appInsights: null }` and telemetry is disabled
3. `enableAutoRouteTracking: true` — App Insights captures every React Router navigation as a page view
4. `disablePageUnloadEvents: ['unload']` — prevents beacon requests on page close (avoids race conditions with SPA navigation)

**The `ai` export**: Every `<ErrorBoundary appInsights={ai.reactPlugin}>` in the app uses this singleton's `reactPlugin`. `AppLogger` uses `ai.appInsights` for structured trace/exception logging.

**Gotcha**: `ai.reactPlugin` is cast as `ReactPlugin` in `AuthenticatedElement.tsx` and `WizardStep.tsx` because the return type of `createTelemetryService` allows null. If App Insights fails to initialize (e.g., missing connection string), `reactPlugin` is null and the ErrorBoundary will throw on the cast.

steps.title: CSP — TrustedTypes policy
steps.description:
**Situation**: `TrustedTypes.createTrustedTypePolicy()` is called in `index.tsx` before React renders. It establishes a Content Security Policy guard using the browser's TrustedTypes API.

**Mechanism**: A `'default'` policy is created that intercepts every script URL assignment in the DOM. `createScriptURL` sanitises the URL via `DOMPurify.sanitize()` before returning it. This prevents script injection attacks from reaching the DOM.

**Architecture gap**: `createHTML` and `createScript` callbacks are commented out (lines 11-18) with TODO notes. This means:
- HTML injection via `innerHTML` and similar is not currently mitigated by TrustedTypes
- Script injection via `eval` and similar is not mitigated

Only script *URL* injection (via `src`, `href`, `action` attribute assignments) is currently blocked.

**Implication for migration**: The new Design System platform may introduce new HTML injection surfaces. Before adopting any component library that uses `innerHTML` (e.g., rich text editors, markdown renderers), implement the `createHTML` callback.

steps.title: ErrorBoundary — migrated to functional component
steps.description:
**Situation**: `ErrorBoundary` has been rewritten as a functional component using `react-error-boundary`. The `react-error-boundary` package's `<ErrorBoundary FallbackComponent={...} onError={...}>` replaces the class component. The interface was renamed from `IErrorBoundaryProps` to `ErrorBoundaryProps`. React 19 blocker resolved.

**Previous mechanism** (now replaced): The class component used `getDerivedStateFromError` (static) to set `{ hasError: true }` and `componentDidCatch` to report the exception to App Insights.

**Current mechanism**: `onError` callback receives the error and component info directly as parameters — no class lifecycle methods required. `FallbackComponent={ErrorFallback}` renders the fallback UI when an error is caught.

**Usage sites updated**: `AuthenticatedElement.tsx`, `WizardStep.tsx`, and `WizardRoutedStep.tsx` all use the updated functional `ErrorBoundary`.

**Gotcha**: `ai.reactPlugin` is still cast as `ReactPlugin` in the call sites. If App Insights fails to initialize, `reactPlugin` is null — add a null guard to `AppInsightsService.ts` to return a no-op plugin on initialization failure.

steps.title: Architecture summary — migration readiness
steps.description:
## What you now understand

The NMI Portal is a well-structured React 18 SPA with clear layering:
- **Bootstrap**: MSAL → TrustedTypes → React (provider hierarchy is critical)
- **Auth**: `AuthenticatedElement` composes three guards; `AccountContext` is the user state machine
- **Forms**: `WizardForm` compound component engine handles all multi-step flows
- **Validation**: Yup module augmentation with mandatory side-effect imports
- **Telemetry**: Module-level singleton; route tracking is automatic
- **CSP**: TrustedTypes for script URLs; HTML/script callbacks are TODO

## React 19 Migration Blockers (ranked)

✅ **ErrorBoundary** — DONE: replaced with react-error-boundary functional component
✅ **React.Children.toArray** — DONE: replaced with React.Children.forEach accumulator
3. **Top-level `await` in `index.tsx`** — verify bundler/browser target compatibility
4. **`StrictMode` double-invoke** — all `useEffect`s need cleanup before upgrade
5. **MSAL React plugin** — verify `@azure/msal-react` has a React 19-compatible release

## Design System Migration Surface

1. **Bootstrap 5 → new component library** — `react-bootstrap` usage is widespread; `Layout`, `Dashboard`, all wizard forms
2. **SCSS partials** — `ClientApp/src/styles/` is the full theme; component-level styles are Bootstrap utility classes
3. **Custom Yup validators** — AU business rules must be ported to any new validation library
4. **AccountContext** — AccountContext split into AccountStateCtx/AccountDispatchCtx in Phase 5.1; modal flags moved to ModalContext in Phase 5.2

**Suggested follow-up tour**: Security and Auth Boundaries
